assessment.overall_rationale: The sets reproduce the bile-acid sulfation and lipid-droplet/peroxisomal programs strongly, while the remaining annotations redistribute detoxification, taurine synthesis, and polyol metabolism across broader mixed modules.

pair_scores.rationale: Both describe hepatic detoxification and share aldehyde-, glutathione-, and aldo-keto-dependent Phase II functions, but the right module centers bile acid and hydroxysteroid sulfation rather than the left module's coordinated Phase I/II xenobiotic battery.

The shared Aldh3a2-mediated clearance of lipid-derived aldehydes links the modules, but the right module chiefly concerns fatty-acid oxidation and lipid-droplet storage rather than xenobiotic detoxification.
These modules share only a broad hepatic metabolic and stress-response context, with no matching central mechanism or predicted output.
Both center Sult2a8-dependent hepatic bile-acid sulfation and sterol elimination, while the left adds taurine synthesis and the right broadens into hydroxysteroid and xenobiotic conjugation.
Bile-acid and sterol homeostasis provides limited physiological context, but sulfation and taurine conjugation differ from the right module's lipid-droplet and fatty-acid oxidation mechanisms.

Both invoke Cdo1-driven cysteine-to-taurine metabolism supporting taurine-conjugated bile acids, but the right module omits sulfotransferase biotransformation and adds unrelated nitrogen, heme, carbohydrate, and aging functions.
Both concern hepatic lipid handling, but the left centers lipid droplets and fatty-acid oxidation whereas the right centers sulfation and Phase II conjugation.
Both define the same hepatic lipid-droplet and peroxisomal fatty-acid oxidation program through Fitm1, Hao2, Cyb5b, and Dgat2, with each adding secondary metabolic components.
Both include Sord-mediated sorbitol-to-fructose metabolism, but this is only one subcomponent within otherwise distinct lipid-homeostasis and mixed catabolic programs.
